steps: Point both index fingers upward with your other fingers curled into loose fists.
Hold both hands in front of your torso at about chest height.
Twist your wrists as you trace two small upward arcs through the air.
Let each fingertip draw a loose cursive W shape, moving upward and outward.
Keep both palms angled toward each other with the fingers leading the motion.
Pair the sign with a bright, satisfied expression to show a good outcome.
tip: The two upward fingertip arcs sketch a cursive W — Lifeprint glosses this sign SUCCEED.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand flat and steady at chest height, palm facing down.
Raise your dominant hand slightly above and a few inches behind the base hand.
Keep the dominant hand in a flat shape with its palm angled downward.
Bring the dominant hand forward over the base hand in one quick motion.
End with a firm stop above the base hand, as if hitting an invisible ceiling.
Use a decisive facial expression — this sign marks a hard upper limit.
tip: Think of the moving hand smacking an invisible ceiling — that firm stop is the maximum.

steps: Start with your dominant hand a few inches in front of your chest.
Shape the hand like a loose grip, as if about to unscrew a light bulb.
Move the hand inward until the thumb side approaches your chest.
Close the fingers into a flattened O as the hand reaches your body.
End with the flat of your thumbnail touching your chest, fingertips meeting.
Keep a matter-of-fact expression; this sign claims possession of something.
tip: It grew out of the fingerspelled O-W-N — the flattened O lands on the chest.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand out as a flat five hand, palm facing sideways.
Reach over with your dominant hand and grasp the non-dominant fingers lightly.
Pull the grasped hand forward in a short, steady tug toward your front.
Release and repeat the pull once more to show more than one guide.
Keep both movements smooth and even, like leading someone by the hand.
Face the direction of travel with an attentive, helpful expression.
tip: One pull leads one person; the repeated tug marks the plural — people who lead.

steps: Shape your dominant hand into an R by crossing your middle finger over your index finger.
Touch the R-hand to one corner of your chin, palm facing inward.
Move the hand across to touch the other corner of your chin.
Repeat the chin-to-chin sweep once more to show more than one place.
Keep the palm facing inward toward your face through both short moves.
Use the same neutral expression as the eating signs — you are naming places to eat.
tip: Same mouth-corner path as EAT; the repeated sweep turns one restaurant into many.

steps: Form a loose four hand with your dominant hand, fingers together and thumb tucked.
Hold the hand beside your lower cheek, near the chin, palm facing sideways.
Shake the hand downward twice in two small, quick strokes.
Keep the strokes short — about an inch — right against the cheek.
Use a neutral expression; context separates this from the color brown.
Some signers circle a W handshape at the cheek instead — know both, use the common one.
tip: Lifeprint glosses WINE the same as BEER — two quick shakes beside the lower cheek.

steps: Press your fingertips against your thumb to form a flattened O handshape.
Bring the flattened O up beside one side of your nose.
Touch lightly as if holding a blossom under your nose to smell it.
Move the hand to the other side of your nose and touch again.
Keep the hand relaxed and the palm angled down toward the face.
Pair the sign with a pleasant expression, as if enjoying the scent.
tip: One touch smells a single flower; touching both sides of the nose shows many.

steps: Point both index fingers upward with your other fingers folded into fists.
Raise both hands to face level, in front of your eyes.
Slide the index fingers up and down past each other in an alternating rhythm.
Turn both palms to face forward, away from your face.
Look up at your hands and toward the imagined sky while you sign.
Repeat the rubbing motion several times to show many stars twinkling.
tip: The alternating finger-rub already suggests many; extra repeats make the plural clear.

steps: Hold your non-dominant hand upright at chest height, fingers together and pointing up.
Turn that hand's palm sideways so it stands like a page of paper.
Bend the fingers of your dominant hand at the knuckles, forming a loose bent hand.
Touch the bent fingertips to the top edge of the upright paper hand.
Tap downward along the paper in steps, as if ticking items off a list.
Repeat the downward taps two or three times to show several separate lists.
tip: The base hand is the paper; repeated downward ticks mark each list's items.
